scope: Seven single-sighting Hays grass candidates whose observation source image rights prevented pixel review
reference_policy: Use user-provided Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas as regional trait authority. Modern accounts for post-1999 species/concepts. Do not infer independent Hays species confirmation from iNaturalist agreement votes.
copyright: One CC BY-NC-ND source and six AR/unspecified sources. Record URLs may be linked, but source images not copied or adapted to public GitHub. Seek permission or a separately licensed voucher.

entries.name: Alopecurus carolinianus
entries.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O’Kennon, Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (1999), user-provided Poaceae PDF
entries.flora_concept: Annual 7–35 cm tall; ligule membrane 3.5–7 mm; narrow head 2–6 cm long and 4–6 mm thick; silky one-flowered spikelets; lemma awn 3–5 mm from near base.
entries.distinguishing: Ligule length, one-flowered silky glumes and geniculate dorsal lemma awn are required, not just a cylindrical head.
entries.comparison: Other Alopecurus and narrow seedheaded grasses
entries.needs: Permission to examine source photo directly or a separate authorized specimen; macro of head, spikelet and ligule.

entries.name: Cenchrus setaceus
entries.source: Kew POWO / GrassBase account under Pennisetum setaceum
entries.flora_concept: Tufted perennial, ligule of hairs, linear cylindrical plumose panicle; individual spikelets approximately 5–7 mm; bristles with plumose hairs.
entries.distinguishing: Scaled spikelet and bristle morphology, not simply a fountain-shaped plume.
entries.comparison: Cenchrus longisetus, Cenchrus alopecuroides and other ornamental Cenchrus
entries.needs: Review original photo with permission or inspect a fresh specimen; check planting and escape context.

entries.name: Digitaria californica
entries.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O’Kennon, Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (1999), user-provided Poaceae PDF
entries.flora_concept: Perennial 50–100 cm tall; digitate or nearly digitate densely flowered branches; second glume and lower-floret margins bearing silky hairs 2–4 mm long.
entries.distinguishing: Long silky spikelet hairs and densely flowered racemes must be visible; identify the actual plant as perennial.
entries.comparison: Other Digitaria, especially non-silky digitate species
entries.needs: Inspect iNaturalist record directly if permitted, or obtain scaled spikelet-hair macro and full rooted plant; not automatic from two ID votes.

entries.name: Elymus macgregorii
entries.source: Go Botany Flora Novae Angliae key + North Carolina vascular flora (post-1999 split)
entries.flora_concept: Compared with E. virginicus, glume awns 10–25 mm (vs about 3–10 mm) and spikelets loosely ascending. Early wildrye spikes have about 9–18 nodes separated 4–7 mm; auricles 2–3 mm.
entries.distinguishing: Measure glume awns, spike widths and spike node count; don't conflate with nearby species or historical E. glabriflorus synonym.
entries.comparison: Existing Elymus virginicus, Elymus glabriflorus (alias under Kew), Elymus curvatus
entries.needs: First choice for observer permission due to 12 source photographs; request scale-based glume and spike measurements and habitat context.

entries.name: Lolium × boucheanum
entries.source: Kew POWO accepted hybrid name + project's nomenclature crosswalk
entries.flora_concept: Accepted hybrid name; phenotype may overlap closely with ryegrasses; photo of leaf and spike alone need not demonstrate hybrid ancestry.
entries.distinguishing: Compare the putative hybrid with L. perenne, L. multiflorum and L. rigidum; require experienced taxonomic determination or documented origin.
entries.comparison: Lolium perenne, Lolium multiflorum, Lolium rigidum
entries.needs: Inspect original two images only with permission; keep hybrid-status hold unless exceptional diagnostic or provenance evidence.

entries.name: Panicum dichotomiflorum
entries.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O’Kennon, Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (1999), user-provided Poaceae PDF
entries.flora_concept: Coarse annual culms 1–2 m, erect to trailing; ligule 0.5–1 mm ciliate membrane with hairs about 2 mm; blades usually glabrous; late-season flowering.
entries.distinguishing: Check short membranous/hairy ligule and mature paniculate spikelets against other Panicum spp.
entries.comparison: Panicum capillare, other Panicum with open panicles
entries.needs: Permission to inspect source image or separate voucher; macro of ligule and mature floret plus habitat.

entries.name: Sporobolus cryptandrus
entries.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O’Kennon, Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (1999), user-provided Poaceae PDF
entries.flora_concept: Perennial with 2–4 mm long white hairs tufted at leaf sheath top; panicles often partly enclosed by upper sheath, commonly 15–30 cm long.
entries.distinguishing: Confirm tufts of white hairs where sheath meets blade and how inflorescence emerges from sheath.
entries.comparison: Other Sporobolus, especially grasses with enclosed flowering panicles
entries.needs: Direct image permission or fresh Hays specimen with upper sheath, ligule hairs and full seedhead on same plant.
